transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because my sleep has gotten really unreliable. Even when I go to bed exhausted, I end up lying there thinking through sales forecasts and team issues, and then I’ll wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning and just… can’t get my brain to shut off again.
When you're lying awake thinking about work, do these thoughts tend to make you feel down, hopeless, or overly critical of yourself?

I’m not sure I’d call it hopeless. It’s more like I get caught up in what I still need to fix or handle. I do second-guess myself sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed it turning into feeling down so much as just tense and stuck thinking.
Do you find that your worry or anxiety about work or other issues feels persistent and hard to control, even when there’s no immediate deadline or crisis?

Yes, it does. I can tell myself, “Brenda, you’ve already made the plan, just let it go,” but then a few minutes later I’m right back in it. It’s like I check one concern off and three more show up, even if nothing urgent is actually happening.
Besides trouble sleeping, have you noticed any other physical signs of stress or anxiety, like restlessness, feeling easily fatigued, difficulty concentrating, irritability, or muscle tension?

Yes. I feel really wound up most of the time, even when I’m not at work. Like I can be sitting at home eating dinner and still feel like I’m in a pipeline review. And my shoulders are almost always tight, even when I’m trying to relax.
How long have you been experiencing this constant worry and physical tension, and does it seem to happen more days than not?
It’s been going on for a while now. I’d say it really started building after the sales division reorganization, about thirteen months ago. And yes, it’s more days than not at this point.
Have these sleep problems and constant worries started to interfere with your ability to perform at work or enjoy your time at home?

Yes, it has. At work I’m second-guessing myself so much that even routine pipeline reviews feel tense and take more out of me than they should. And then when I get home, I’m just drained. I’m more reactive than I want to be, and I’m not really present with my husband the way I used to be.

Have you ever experienced sudden episodes where you feel intense fear or discomfort that peaks within minutes, maybe with symptoms like a racing heart, shortness of breath, or feeling like you’re losing control?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get really anxious and tense, but I wouldn’t say it suddenly peaks within minutes like an attack or that I feel like I’m losing control. It’s more just kind of constant.
Have you noticed these anxious feelings even in situations where there’s no specific stressor or challenge to deal with, or does it always seem tied to things like work pressures or responsibilities?

It’s usually tied to something, but the “something” can be pretty small. Most days my mind jumps around—from whether we’ll hit the launch numbers, to whether someone on my team might quit, then the mortgage or a client renewal. Even a small delay can start feeling like it’s going to turn into something bigger.
Do you ever feel anxious or on edge even when there isn't anything specific going on or something you're actively worried about?

Yeah, I do. Even when nothing is really happening, I still feel wound up, like I’m bracing for something. I can be sitting at home eating dinner and my body feels like I’m still in a tense work meeting. My shoulders stay tight, and it’s hard to actually relax.
Even in moments when there’s no immediate pressure or external stress, do you still find yourself feeling anxious or physically tense?

Yes. Even when there’s no real pressure, I still feel wound up a lot of the time. Like I can be at home eating dinner, and my body feels like I’m still sitting in a tense pipeline review at work. My shoulders stay tight, and I can’t really get myself to relax.
Would you say that your anxiety and tense feelings are present nearly every day, as opposed to coming and going depending on stressors?

Yeah, I’d say it’s nearly every day. It doesn’t really just switch off when the stressor is gone. I feel wound up most of the time, like I’m still in a tense work meeting even if I’m just at home having dinner. My shoulders stay tight, and relaxing takes a lot of effort.
Have you noticed your mood feeling low or flat, not just tense or anxious, where things you usually enjoy feel less rewarding or you feel more hopeless or guilty than usual?

I don’t think so, not in a clear way. I mean, I get worn down from feeling tense all the time, but I wouldn’t say things feel hopeless or that I don’t enjoy anything. It’s more anxiety than feeling depressed, I think.

Do you find that your anxiety and worry extend beyond work-related concerns, such as worrying excessively about everyday things like health, family, or minor responsibilities, and do you feel like it's really hard to stop worrying, even when you know it's not productive?

Yes, it does go beyond work. I’ll worry about small responsibilities or random things, and even when I know I’ve already thought it through, I can’t really shut it off. I’ll tell myself, “Brenda, you’ve made the plan, let it go,” but five minutes later I’m back in another loop. It’s like I check one concern off and then three more pop up.
On nights when you’re feeling particularly anxious, does it take you a long time to actually fall asleep, or do you find yourself waking up multiple times throughout the night?

Yes, both, really. Even when I’m exhausted, I’ll get into bed and just lie there replaying sales forecasts or team issues in my head. And then if I do fall asleep, I often wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning and can’t get my brain to shut back down.

Do you find that your anxiety and physical symptoms, like feeling wound up or muscle tension, show up in situations outside of work, such as during leisure activities, time with friends, or other non-work-related moments?

Yes, it definitely shows up outside of work too. Even at home, like if I’m just eating dinner or trying to relax, I still feel wound up, almost like I’m sitting in a pipeline review. My shoulders stay tight a lot of the time, even when I’m not doing anything stressful.
Would you say that your excessive worry and anxiety have occurred on more days than not for at least six months?

Yes. It’s been more days than not, for sure. I’d say it really started building after the sales division reorganization, which was about thirteen months ago now. Since then it’s just been kind of constant.
